findings.detail: The row reflects the December 31, 2022 comparative schedule and captured the parenthetical EUR fair value 6,864 instead of the dollar fair value 7,326.
For the cited row, fair_value_currency is U_EUR even though the source Fair Value column is dollar-denominated and the EUR amount is only parenthetical disclosure.

rationale: FX02 is a Class 1 single-cell currency-unit check. The raw schedule's Fair Value column is USD-denominated; table 9 row 8 shows a dollar fair value of 7,326 with a parenthetical EUR 6,864. The reviewed extracted row has fair_value_currency U_EUR and fair_value 6,864 for that instrument, so the stored fair-value currency/value follows the parenthetical foreign-currency disclosure rather than the USD fair-value column. This grounds a real extraction/comparative leak error. Some U_USD rows may only reflect unit-code normalization noise, but the cited U_EUR row is an independently grounded defect.
